content:
{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Primary endpoint analysis lacks estimand attributes",
      "quote": "The pCR rate per independent central pathology review along with 95% exact confidence interval will be calculated using Clopper-Pearson method",
      "page": 74,
      "section": "11.5.3.1",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The analysis description for the primary endpoint does not specify the estimand attributes: population (FAS is stated elsewhere but not here), variable definition (pCR rate), intercurrent events handling (e.g., patients who do not undergo surgery), and summary measure (rate with CI). The protocol lacks a formal estimand framework.",
      "fix": "Add an estimand section for the primary endpoint specifying population, variable, intercurrent events (e.g., treatment discontinuation, no surgery) and handling strategies, and summary measure."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing analysis for secondary endpoints EFS, DFS, OS",
      "quote": "Event free survival (EFS), DFS and OS will be summarized using Kaplan-Meier method.",
      "page": 74,
      "section": "11.5.3.2",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The analysis for EFS, DFS, and OS is only described as Kaplan-Meier summaries and descriptive statistics. There is no specification of the estimand (e.g., definition of events, censoring rules, intercurrent events like treatment switching), nor any formal statistical testing or confidence intervals for these time-to-event endpoints.",
      "fix": "Provide detailed statistical methods for EFS, DFS, and OS including event definitions, censoring, and if applicable, hypothesis testing or estimation with confidence intervals."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing analysis for safety endpoints",
      "quote": "Safety and tolerability as measured by the incidence of adverse events (AEs), serious adverse events (SAEs), deaths, and laboratory abnormalities",
      "page": 26,
      "section": "4.2",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The safety endpoint is listed but no statistical analysis method is described in the statistical plan. The plan only mentions descriptive statistics for continuous and categorical variables, but no specific safety analysis (e.g., incidence rates, AE tables) is outlined.",
      "fix": "Add a section on safety analysis methods, including how AEs, SAEs, deaths, and lab abnormalities will be summarized and analyzed."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing analysis for change in surgical and post-surgical management plans",
      "quote": "Change in surgical plan in the screening period versus actual surgery after neoadjuvant cemiplimab",
      "page": 26,
      "section": "4.2",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The secondary endpoints for change in surgical plan and post-surgical management plan are listed, but the statistical methods section only mentions 'Change in planned surgery' without details. There is no description of how these changes will be analyzed (e.g., descriptive statistics, paired tests, or agreement measures).",
      "fix": "Provide explicit statistical methods for analyzing changes in surgical and post-surgical management plans, including the summary measure and any inferential tests."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing analysis for exploratory endpoints",
      "quote": "The exploratory endpoints are: Patterns of failure ... Change in estimated costs ... Incidence of ADA ... Health-related quality of life",
      "page": 26,
      "section": "4.3",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The exploratory endpoints are listed but no statistical analysis methods are described for them in the statistical plan. The plan only covers primary and secondary efficacy analyses, and safety is not detailed. There is no mention of how patterns of failure, cost changes, ADA incidence, or QoL will be analyzed.",
      "fix": "Add a section for exploratory analyses describing methods for each exploratory endpoint."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing handling of missing data",
      "quote": "For continuous variables, descriptive statistics will include the following information: the number of patients reflected in the calculation (n), mean, standard deviation, Q1, median, Q3, minimum, and maximum.",
      "page": 74,
      "section": "11.5",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The statistical plan does not describe how missing data will be handled for any endpoint. For the primary endpoint, patients who do not undergo surgery or have missing pathology results are not addressed. For time-to-event endpoints, censoring is not defined. For QoL and other endpoints, missing data imputation is not specified.",
      "fix": "Add a section on missing data handling, including for the primary endpoint (e.g., non-responder imputation) and for time-to-event and QoL endpoints."
    },
    {
      "title": "No multiplicity control for secondary endpoints",
      "quote": "The secondary endpoints are: mPR rate ... pCR rate and mPR rate ... ORR ... EFS, DFS, OS ... Safety ... Change in surgical plan ... Change in post-surgical management plan",
      "page": 26,
      "section": "4.2",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The protocol does not describe any multiplicity adjustment for the multiple secondary endpoints. Since several endpoints are tested (e.g., pCR, mPR, ORR, EFS, DFS, OS), the type I error rate may be inflated. The statistical plan does not mention hierarchical testing or other methods.",
      "fix": "Specify a multiplicity control strategy for secondary endpoints, such as hierarchical testing or a fixed sequence, or state that no adjustment is made and justify."
    },
    {
      "title": "Sample size inconsistency: 72 vs 76 patients",
      "quote": "Seventy-two (72) patients will be required to provide 90% power ... The sample size will be further increased by 5% to account for patients who prematurely withdraw from the study. Hence, the total sample size will be approximately 76 patients.",
      "page": 72,
      "section": "11.2",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The sample size calculation states 72 patients are required, then increased by 5% to 76. However, 72 * 1.05 = 75.6, which rounds to 76, but the text says 'approximately 76' which is fine. The inconsistency is that the power calculation is based on 72, but the final sample size is 76, which may slightly increase power. This is not a major issue but should be clarified.",
      "fix": "Clarify that the sample size of 76 accounts for 5% inflation and that power is based on 72 evaluable patients."
    }
  ]
}
